application.cv_markdown:
Sven Muller

Contact: sven.muller@mail.example | Stockholm / willing to relocate

Summary

Senior signal processing engineer with 25 years in radar systems. Led a team of eight DSP engineers as Head of Signal Processing at Nordkom Radar Systems in 2020–2021. Deep expertise in phased-array design, embedded firmware, and RF measurement.

Education

MSc Electrical Engineering — Roslagen Royal Institute of Technology, 2000

Work Experience

Signal Processing Engineer — Nordkom Radar Systems, Stockholm, 2001–present

Core individual-contributor role in Nordkom's radar signal-processing group.

- Designed the digital beamforming architecture for Nordkom's naval X-band surveillance radar: a 64-element planar array with sum/difference beamforming and adaptive sidelobe cancellation. Wrote the real-time beamformer firmware in C on a TI TMS320C6678 multi-core DSP, meeting the 10-microsecond pulse-repetition-interval timing constraint. This module has been in production since 2009.
- Implemented the pulse-compression and Doppler processing chain for the same radar, in C++, running on the same multi-core DSP platform. Responsible for the full embedded software lifecycle from architecture through unit test through field-integration support.
- Built the production Python integration-test framework for Nordkom's radar signal-processing boards: instrument control (SCPI over Ethernet to signal generators and spectrum analysers), automated test-sequence execution, and pass/fail reporting. Approximately 8,000 lines, pytest-covered, maintained since 2015, used by the test and verification team daily.
- Supported Nordkom's work on an airborne maritime-surveillance radar for a Nordic defence customer. My role was the signal-processing specification and acceptance testing of the airborne receiver module, which involved verifying performance at altitude-simulated thermal conditions.
- Swedish citizen, EU work authorisation.

Projects

Nordkom–Gotaalv Antenna Measurement Collaboration (2016–2017)

Designed the measurement protocol and performed all data collection for a joint Nordkom-Gotaalv antenna characterisation campaign. Work included calibration of a 16-element sub-array using a Keysight PNA-X in Gotaalv's spherical near-field measurement facility, and comparison of measured vs. simulated element patterns. My electrical engineering training (RRIT, array theory and electromagnetics coursework) was directly applied in the analysis phase. Results contributed to a Gotaalv master's thesis but were not separately published.

Nordkom–Suvanto Oulu Receiver Characterisation (2019)

Contributed to a two-week measurement campaign at Suvanto's Oulu facility, performing receiver characterisation and calibration cross-checks for a naval communications programme. The work gave me direct familiarity with Oulu's engineering environment. My wife is from Raahe and we have family in the Oulu region, and the decision to pursue opportunities there was already forming at that point. We have since confirmed our availability and explored housing and schools.

Skills

- Phased-array beamforming, adaptive sidelobe cancellation
- Embedded DSP firmware (C/C++, TI C6000 family)
- Radar signal processing (pulse compression, Doppler, CFAR)
- RF measurement, antenna characterisation
- S. Muller, J. Lindqvist, "Efficient Subarray-Level Digital Beamforming for Shipborne X-band Radar," Proc. SESE Radar Conference, 2013. Also: two internal Nordkom technical reports on adaptive clutter cancellation (2010, 2015), used as reference documents within the naval radar programme.
- English — all Nordkom engineering documentation, customer interface documents, and NTA agreement-referenced test reports written in English; presented at SESE Radar Conference (2013) and Baltic Radar Conference (2017) in English.
- MATLAB, Simulink, VHDL

Languages

Swedish (native), English (professional), German (conversational)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Sven Muller
Stockholm
sven.muller@mail.example

Kaikuvaara Oy — Senior Signal Processing Engineer

Twenty-five years at Nordkom Radar Systems is the short version of my background. The longer version is in the CV, but the highlights are a 64-element naval radar beamformer that has been in production since 2009, an 8,000-line Python integration-test framework the verification team uses daily, and embedded DSP firmware on TI multi-core platforms delivered under hard real-time constraints.

The concrete deliverables I have shipped at Nordkom cover the full radar signal-processing chain: phased-array beamforming, pulse compression, Doppler processing, and the test infrastructure around all of it. I also have applied experience with Kalman filtering and estimation theory, which I understand is relevant to the kind of instrument work Kaikuvaara does.

I have supported airborne radar work as well — specifically the signal-processing specification and acceptance testing for Nordkom's maritime surveillance radar — so I understand the constraints that come with platform-mounted systems, though my core experience is ground-segment and naval.

On the practical side: my wife is from Raahe and we have been planning a move to the Oulu region for family reasons. I participated in a measurement campaign at Suvanto Oulu in 2019 and I know the local engineering environment. This is not a speculative relocation — we have already looked at housing and schools. I am a Swedish citizen with full EU work authorisation.

I would be glad to discuss the details in a meeting.

Sven Muller

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
